title: TechStep Mock Interview Workshop [Auckland In-person Event]
location: AUT WG Building, WG801 and WG 808, Auckland
description:
The Mock Interview Workshop is a structured career development initiative designed to support people from under-represented communities to successfully enter or progress within digital and technology careers in New Zealand.
Industry professionals will be invited as table hosts to facilitate small-group mock interviews, including:

title: Using Copilot for Design and Actions Workflows
description:
We are back for another edition of the GitHub User Group. This month we dive into using Copilot and AI to enhance the design workflow, and look at how we can leverage AI in our GitHub Actions.

**Product Design with Source Control: Using GitHub, AI, and Preview Builds as Your Source of Truth \~ [Walt Lim](https://www.linkedin.com/in/waltzaround/)**

In this talk, Walt shares how he uses GitHub and AI to rethink the design process, moving beyond traditional prototypes to code as the source of truth. By using pull requests and ephemeral preview builds, he creates fast, realistic, and testable environments where ideas can be reviewed, iterated, and validated in context. Combined with AI-assisted workflows, this approach helps his team move quicker, reduce ambiguity, and make better decisions with less overhead

**From One PR to Another: Agentic Workflows on GitHub \~ [Sinan Nar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sinannar/)**

A live demo of using AI-driven workflows to trigger actions across repositories—automatically creating a PR in a second repo when changes are merged.
bio: Sinan is an Apps and AI Consultant at ARINCO, a Microsoft and GitHub partner consultancy. He co-organises the Aotearoa Azure User Group and the Auckland .NET User Group. An experienced and certified software engineer, he specialises in the Microsoft ecosystem, with a focus on Azure and GitHub.

title: Mother's Day sewing repair café
location: Freemans Bay Community Centre, 52 Hepburn Street, Freemans Bay, Auckland, Auckland
description:
This Mother’s Day, we’re celebrating the threads that connect us - across time, across generations and through the clothes we cherish.
Join Fashion Revolution New Zealand and Repair Café Aotearoa New Zealand for a special sewing Repair Café, Generations of Care, taking place on the Saturday before Mother’s Day. This gathering is an invitation to slow down, sit side-by-side, and mend - not just garments, but stories, memories and connections.
Repairing and mending are more than just fixing an object - they are a legacy of wisdom passed down through the hands of our mothers, aunties, and grandmothers. It is the restorative power of mending memories and ensuring that the things we love - and the skills to save them - are carried forward to the next generation.
Bring along a piece that holds meaning: a well-worn favourite, a treasured heirloom, or something passed down from your mum or grandmother. Our skilled volunteers will mend your item and share their knowledge. This is a space to honour the care woven into clothing across generations.
Come with your mum, your grandmother or someone who feels like home. And for those whose mothers are no longer with us, you’re warmly invited to join us in remembrance - bring a special keepsake and mend it in honour of mum, holding her memory in every stitch.
We’re also delighted to be collaborating with Ozone Coffee, just nearby. Make a morning of it and enjoy breakfast or lunch before or after the Repair Cafe, continuing the ritual of care, connection and conversation.
Bring a garment or textile in need of a little aroha (and maybe your mum, too).
Let’s mend with meaning - for the people we love and for the clothes that carry their stories.

Modern software delivery is accelerating faster than traditional QA can keep up. Teams are facing rising costs, delayed releases and significant reputational risks when quality is compromised. At the same time, AI-generated code and rapid release cycles are outpacing manual testing capabilities.

This session explores how autonomous, cloud-native QA powered by AI agents is transforming software verification—reducing testing time from days to minutes and costs from thousands to tens of dollars, supported by AWS Well-Architected principles of:

Operational Excellence: Automating QA workflows with self-service, zero-setup AI agents
Reliability: Detecting broken links, errors and performance issues before production
Cost Optimization: Moving from high fixed QA costs to on-demand, per-run pricing models and more

title: NZTrio: Dreamscape
location: Warkworth Town Hall, 2 Alnwick Street, Warkworth, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Dreamscape traverses vivid musical worlds where memory and imagination converge.
Roxanna Panufnik’s Around Three Corners opens with rich textures and unexpected harmonies then Robert Schumann’s Piano Trio No. 1 in d minor follows, full of Romantic passion and lyrical depth.
The intimate connection between performer and instrument is explored with inventive, tactile sounds in Claire Cowan’s wood : strings : hammers : flesh, before Charles Ives’ boldly original Piano Trio, blending American folk tunes, raucous humour and experimental techniques into a collage that is by turns nostalgic and witty.

Roxanna Panufnik - Around Three Corners
Robert Schumann - Piano Trio No. 1 in d minor
Claire Cowan (NZ) - wood : strings : hammers : flesh
Charles Ives - Piano Trio

This concert features guest pianist Jian Liu.
Duration: approximately 105 minutes including 20 minute interval.

title: The Lamplighters
location: Howick Little Theatre, 1 Sir Lloyd Drive, Pakuranga, Auckland 2010, Auckland
description:
By the creator and writer of Taggart comes The Lamplighters:
In a remote Cumbrian farmhouse, three former detectives reunite on the anniversary of a murder case that still haunts them. When they are joined by a determined young crime writer who is unwilling to let the past lie, old loyalties splinter and buried secrets start to surface. As mist closes in and the night deepens, their friendship falters and after 10 years the truth may finally emerge.
Recommended for ages 16+. Contains strong language and adult themes.

title: Stoicism & Spirituality: Master Yourself… or Let Go of Yourself?
location: 37 Normanby Road, Mount Eden, Auckland 1024, Auckland
description:
**Two ancient systems. One modern problem: how to live well.**
Stoicism teaches control, discipline, and self-mastery.
Spiritual traditions teach surrender, acceptance, and release.
Are they fundamentally opposed—or just different paths to the same outcome?

**Stoicism = control of the self**
**Spirituality = surrender of the self**
They sound like opposites—but both promise the same thing: peace.
So which actually works?

Join us for a fast-paced, thought-provoking discussion where we put these two philosophies head-to-head (in small groups) and see what survives.

Bonus fun ...
... are these quotes from Stoics or Eastern spiritualists?

* "He who conquers others is strong; he who conquers himself is mighty"
* "God is near you, he is with you, he is within you."
